AutoMountDrives.Description: Finds every fixed internal partition with a mountable filesystem (ext4/btrfs/xfs/f2fs/ntfs/exfat/vfat) that isn't already handled, and adds a permanent /etc/fstab entry mounting it at a stable /mnt/<label> path with 'nofail' — the right place for a second games/data NVMe, so Steam libraries and symlinks never move. Skips the OS/boot/swap disks, anything already in fstab, LUKS, and removable media. NTFS uses the in-kernel ntfs3 driver with your uid/gid so games are writable. Reversible: undo unmounts and strips exactly the block it added (and migrates off any older /run/media setup a previous version made).

CstateFix.Description: Adds processor.max_cstate=1 to the kernel boot params. The 5800H's deep C-states (C6) are unstable on this board and cause random full-system freezes. Requires reboot to take effect.

IdleNomwait.Description: Alternative to the C-state fix above — skips the mwait idle driver entirely. Try this INSTEAD of the C-state fix if that one doesn't resolve freezes, not in addition to it. Requires reboot.

ClocksourceTsc.Description: Forces the CPU's own timestamp counter instead of the motherboard's HPET as the system timer. Helps timing jitter on some boards, does nothing on others. Requires reboot.

UsbAutosuspend.Description: Stops Linux from power-suspending USB ports, fixing wireless mouse/controller dongles or headsets that lag or briefly disconnect.

MouseAccelFlat.Description: 1:1 mouse movement, no acceleration curve — applies under X11. Under Wayland/KDE Plasma (Nobara's default) also set System Settings > Mouse > Acceleration Profile to Flat.
apply:
printf 'Section "InputClass"
    Identifier "Flat pointer accel"
    MatchIsPointer "on"
    Driver "libinput"
    Option "AccelProfile" "flat"
    Option "AccelSpeed" "0"
EndSection
' > /etc/X11/xorg.conf.d/50-mouse-accel.conf

Swappiness.Description: Keeps RAM from being swapped out while games/mods are open. Pairs well with the zram tweak below.

ZramTune.Description: Fedora/Nobara already runs zram-generator by default — this bumps its size fraction for heavier gaming loads.

BalooDisable.Description: Stops background file content indexing — the single biggest idle CPU/disk drain on stock Plasma. Applied for your user account.

PowerProfileScripts.Description: Two one-word commands that emulate the Windows G-key: 'gaming-performance' sets the 'performance' platform_profile (= G-Mode: firmware ramps the fan curve + raises CPU/GPU power limits) AND slams the alienware-wmi fan boost to max, like AWCC does; 'gaming-balanced' undoes both. These are what the tray icon, the G-key listener and the Dashboard toggle call.
apply:
cat > /usr/local/bin/gaming-performance <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
powerprofilesctl set performance
# G-Mode fan slam (AWCC-style): max the alienware-wmi fan boost
for h in /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*; do
  [ "$(cat "$h/name" 2>/dev/null)" = alienware_wmi ] || continue
  for b in "$h"/fan[0-9]*_boost; do [ -w "$b" ] && echo 255 > "$b"; done
done
exit 0
SCRIPT

cat > /usr/local/bin/gaming-balanced <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
powerprofilesctl set balanced
for h in /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*; do
  [ "$(cat "$h/name" 2>/dev/null)" = alienware_wmi ] || continue
  for b in "$h"/fan[0-9]*_boost; do [ -w "$b" ] && echo 0 > "$b"; done
done
exit 0
SCRIPT

TlpEnable.Description: Mature laptop power/thermal tuning for the 5800H. Disables power-profiles-daemon to avoid the two fighting over the CPU governor. Pick this OR the auto-cpufreq app below, not both.

AmdgpuPerfScripts.Description: Forces the AMD Vega iGPU to its highest DPM performance level on demand (Linux equivalent of disabling AMD ULPS on Windows). Only matters if you're rendering on the iGPU.

NvidiaMaxPerf.Description: Enables NVIDIA persistence mode + prefers max PowerMizer performance, avoiding clock-transition stutter at the cost of power/heat. Run it before a session.
apply:
printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash
nvidia-smi -pm 1 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
if [[ -n "${DISPLAY:-}" ]] && command -v nvidia-settings >/dev/null; then nvidia-settings -a "[gpu:0]/GpuPowerMizerMode=1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
exit 0
' > /usr/local/bin/nvidia-max-perf

ControllerUdev.Description: Non-root access to Xbox/PlayStation/generic HID pads. Usually already covered by the Steam package — this is a fallback.
apply:
printf 'SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTRS{idVendor}=="045e", MODE="0666"
SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTRS{idVendor}=="054c", MODE="0666"
SUBSYSTEM=="hidraw", MODE="0666"
' > /etc/udev/rules.d/99-gamepads.rules

HotkeyListener.Description: Installs a systemd user service that listens for the dedicated G-key (confirmed on the G15 5515 to send KEY_PERFORMANCE when Fn Lock is OFF) and toggles Game Mode on press — same effect as clicking the tray icon. Requires PowerProfileScripts/AmdgpuPerfScripts/NvidiaMaxPerf above to be installed first, and python3-evdev. Adds your user to the 'input' group so the service can read the keyboard device — log out and back in once after applying for that to take effect.
HotkeyListener.check: sudo -u {USER} XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u {USER}) systemctl --user is-enabled tuxthrottle-hotkey.service 2>/dev/null | grep -q enabled && id -nG {USER} | grep -qw input
undo: sudo -u {USER} XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u {USER}) systemctl --user disable --now tuxthrottle-hotkey.service 2>/dev/null || true

PasswordlessGameModeToggle.Description: Lets the tray icon and the G-key listener flip Game Mode without a password prompt every single press. Scoped ONLY to the five specific toggle scripts, not general root access. Skip this if you'd rather approve each toggle via a GUI polkit prompt.

RaplPowerPermissions.Description: Linux locks CPU package power counters (RAPL, under /sys/class/powercap) to root-only by default since 2020 (a side-channel security mitigation) — without this, the Dashboard tab and the tray icon (which deliberately run unprivileged) can never show real CPU wattage, always 'n/a'. Adds a udev rule making them world-readable, the same fix MangoHud's own docs recommend for its power display. Note: Nobara 43 already ships these files world-readable, so this is usually a no-op there — apply it only if the Dashboard actually shows 'n/a' for CPU wattage. Trade-off: makes RAPL energy counters readable by any local user/process, a known but low-severity timing side-channel — standard practice on gaming-focused distros/tools, not enabled by default here.

MangoHudGlobalToggle.Description: Turns MangoHud into a system-wide overlay instead of something you paste into each game's Steam launch options one at a time. Installs 'mangohud-global-on'/'mangohud-global-off', which write/remove ~/.config/environment.d/mangohud.conf (MANGOHUD=1 + LD_PRELOAD for the rare pure-OpenGL title — Vulkan games pick it up via the implicit-layer 'enable_environment' mechanism from MANGOHUD=1 alone, no LD_PRELOAD needed there). Takes effect on next login (or next Steam/game launch after restarting your session) since it's a systemd environment.d file, not a live env var. Once active, MangoHud's own in-game keybind (Shift_R+F12 by default) shows/hides the overlay display without disabling the underlying hook. Requires the GameModeMangoHud app installed first.
apply:
cat > /usr/local/bin/mangohud-global-on <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/environment.d
cat > ~/.config/environment.d/mangohud.conf <<'CONF'
MANGOHUD=1
LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib64/mangohud/libMangoHud.so
CONF
echo 'MangoHud enabled globally - log out/in (or relaunch Steam) for it to apply to new games.'
SCRIPT

cat > /usr/local/bin/mangohud-global-off <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
rm -f ~/.config/environment.d/mangohud.conf
echo 'MangoHud global toggle removed - log out/in (or relaunch Steam) for it to fully clear.'
SCRIPT

KernelGamingCmdline.Description: Adds a curated, hardware-appropriate subset of the usual gaming kernel cmdline: split_lock_detect=off + split_lock_mitigate=0 (no stalls on misaligned locked ops — common in games/emulators), nowatchdog + nosoftlockup (drop the per-second watchdog timer/IRQ), timer_migration=0 (keep timers on their own CPU), preempt=full (fully preemptible — this Nobara kernel is PREEMPT_DYNAMIC so it takes the switch), threadirqs (threaded IRQ handlers, better audio/input latency), ignore_rlimit_data (some Wine/DXVK builds need it), sysrq_always_enabled=1, audit=0. Deliberately EXCLUDES the Intel-only / laptop-dangerous entries from typical desktop lists (intel_pstate=disable is a no-op on this AMD CPU; thermal.off=1, nomce, vdso=0, nohz_full=all left out on purpose). Requires reboot.
apply: grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="sysrq_always_enabled=1 split_lock_detect=off split_lock_mitigate=0 nowatchdog nosoftlockup timer_migration=0 preempt=full threadirqs ignore_rlimit_data audit=0"
undo: grubby --update-kernel=ALL --remove-args="sysrq_always_enabled=1 split_lock_detect=off split_lock_mitigate=0 nowatchdog nosoftlockup timer_migration=0 preempt=full threadirqs ignore_rlimit_data audit=0"

Ipv6DisableCmdline.Description: Adds ipv6.disable=1 to the kernel cmdline — matches the setup this config was ported from. Only do this if you know nothing on your network needs IPv6 (some VPNs, Tailscale MagicDNS, and a few games' matchmaking prefer it). Requires reboot.

CpuMaxPerformance.Content: Force CPU performance governor at boot
CpuMaxPerformance.Description: Installs a oneshot systemd service (tuxthrottle-cpu-perf.service) that pins every core to the 'performance' governor and energy_performance_preference=performance on boot — the amd_pstate 'active' driver on the 5800H only exposes performance/powersave, so this is the max-clocks setting. NOTE: power-profiles-daemon rewrites the governor whenever you switch power profile (or use the Game Mode toggle), so this mainly helps if you do NOT switch profiles / don't use Game Mode. If you use Game Mode, that already covers it. Reversible.
apply:
cat > /usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-cpu-perf <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
for f in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor; do echo performance > "$f"; done
for f in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/energy_performance_preference; do [ -e "$f" ] && echo performance > "$f"; done
SCRIPT

cat > /etc/systemd/system/tuxthrottle-cpu-perf.service <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=Force CPU performance governor (TuxThrottle)
After=multi-user.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-cpu-perf

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT

BtrfsNoatime.Description: Stops the filesystem writing an access-time stamp on every file read — pure I/O reduction, safe on Btrfs (Nobara's default). Backs up /etc/fstab to /etc/fstab.tuxthrottle-bak first, edits only the ' / ' Btrfs line, and remounts live. Undo restores the backup.

NvmeIoTune.Description: The NVMe scheduler is already 'none' on this system (correct for NVMe), so this only lowers read_ahead_kb to 128 (from 256) — less wasted prefetch on the small random reads typical of game assets. Tiny effect, fully reversible. (nr_requests is left alone: its max is per-device and some queues here reject a bump, which just logs a harmless udev error at boot.)

WifiPowersaveOff.Description: The AX200 has power-save ON by default, which adds latency spikes and occasional stutter to online play. Writes a NetworkManager drop-in (wifi.powersave=2) so it stays off across reconnects. Reversible.
apply: systemctl reload NetworkManager || systemctl restart NetworkManager || true

NetLatencySysctl.Description: Writes /etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxthrottle-net.conf: BBR congestion control + fq qdisc (better behaviour under load / on lossy Wi-Fi), TCP Fast Open, no slow-start-after-idle, bigger backlog and socket buffers. All stock kernel features on Nobara. Reversible.

DnfSpeed.Description: Appends max_parallel_downloads=10 and fastestmirror=True to /etc/dnf/dnf.conf — the dnf equivalent of ranking mirrors. Makes every install/update in this toolkit noticeably faster. Reversible (removes the two lines).

GamingResourceLimits.Description: Wine (esync/fsync), Proton, and shader compilers open huge numbers of file descriptors and memory maps. Sets a hard/soft nofile limit of 1048576 in /etc/security/limits.d and bumps fs.file-max, fs.inotify.max_user_watches, and vm.max_map_count via sysctl. Takes effect on next login for the nofile limit. Reversible.

KbdBacklightFix.Content: Keyboard Backlight: re-apply saved colour at boot/resume
KbdBacklightFix.Description: On the G15 5515 the keyboard backlight is driven through OpenRGB (the AW-ELC has no kernel driver and ignores raw HID writes); the backlight must also be enabled in BIOS setup. This installs tuxthrottle_kbd.py (an openrgb wrapper) to /usr/local/bin, a headless 'openrgb --server' service so colour changes apply in ~1s instead of ~4s, plus a systemd service + a systemd-sleep hook that re-apply ~/.config/tuxthrottle/kbd.json (set in the Keyboard tab) at boot and after resume, since the colour does not persist a power cycle on its own. Requires the OpenRGB app. Reversible.
KbdBacklightFix.check: test -x /usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-kbd && systemctl is-enabled tuxthrottle-kbd.service 2>/dev/null | grep -q enabled && systemctl is-enabled tuxthrottle-openrgb.service 2>/dev/null | grep -q enabled
apply:
cat > /etc/systemd/system/tuxthrottle-openrgb.service <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=OpenRGB SDK server for the Dell G15 keyboard (TuxThrottle)
After=multi-user.target systemd-udev-settle.service

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/bin/openrgb --server --noautoconnect
ExecStartPost=/bin/sh -c 'for i in $(seq 40); do ss -ltn 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":6742 " && break; sleep 0.5; done; exit 0'
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=3
TimeoutStartSec=40

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT

cat > /etc/systemd/system/tuxthrottle-kbd.service <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=Re-apply Dell G15 keyboard backlight (TuxThrottle)
After=multi-user.target systemd-udev-settle.service tuxthrottle-openrgb.service
Wants=tuxthrottle-openrgb.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
Environment=TUXTHROTTLE_KBD_STATE=/home/{USER}/.config/tuxthrottle/kbd.json
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-kbd apply-saved
TimeoutStartSec=150

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT

cat > /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/tuxthrottle-kbd <<'HOOK'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "$1" = post ]; then
  sleep 2
  TUXTHROTTLE_KBD_STATE=/home/{USER}/.config/tuxthrottle/kbd.json /usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-kbd apply-saved || true
fi
HOOK

DesktopLauncher.Description: Installs a .desktop entry (with the flaming-gauge icon) into your application menu / launcher so you can start the Toolkit without a terminal. Points at wherever this repo currently lives. Reversible.

RyzenAdjTDP.Content: CPU TDP control (ryzenadj) + persist across reboot
RyzenAdjTDP.Description: Installs ryzenadj (from the distro repo, or built from source as a fallback) so the Power & Limits tab can set the 5800H's STAPM / fast / slow power limits — the Linux 'ThrottleStop for Ryzen'. Also installs tuxthrottle-tdp (re-applies ~/.config/tuxthrottle/tdp.json), a boot+resume service so your chosen limits survive a reboot, and a narrow sudoers rule so a future CLI/tray can call it without a password. The GUI itself already runs elevated and doesn't need the sudoers rule. Reversible.
RyzenAdjTDP.check: command -v ryzenadj >/dev/null 2>&1 && test -x /usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-tdp && systemctl is-enabled tuxthrottle-tdp.service 2>/dev/null | grep -q enabled
apply: command -v ryzenadj >/dev/null 2>&1 || dnf install -y ryzenadj || true

if ! command -v ryzenadj >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf install -y cmake gcc gcc-c++ make git pciutils-devel && rm -rf /tmp/ryzenadj-build && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/FlyGoat/RyzenAdj /tmp/ryzenadj-build && cmake -S /tmp/ryzenadj-build -B /tmp/ryzenadj-build/build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build /tmp/ryzenadj-build/build && install -m 0755 /tmp/ryzenadj-build/build/ryzenadj /usr/local/bin/ryzenadj; fi

cat > /usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-tdp <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Apply STAPM/fast/slow limits from tdp.json (Watts). Usage: tuxthrottle-tdp [file]
set -e
RA="$(command -v ryzenadj || echo /usr/local/bin/ryzenadj)"
F="${1:-/home/{USER}/.config/tuxthrottle/tdp.json}"
[ -r "$F" ] || { echo "no $F"; exit 0; }
read_key(){ grep -oE "\"$1\"[ ]*:[ ]*[0-9]+" "$F" | grep -oE '[0-9]+$'; }
S=$(read_key stapm); FA=$(read_key fast); SL=$(read_key slow)
ARGS=()
[ -n "$S" ]  && ARGS+=(--stapm-limit=$((S*1000)))
[ -n "$FA" ] && ARGS+=(--fast-limit=$((FA*1000)))
[ -n "$SL" ] && ARGS+=(--slow-limit=$((SL*1000)))
[ ${#ARGS[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo 'nothing to apply'; exit 0; }
exec "$RA" "${ARGS[@]}"
SCRIPT

cat > /etc/systemd/system/tuxthrottle-tdp.service <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=Re-apply saved CPU TDP limits (TuxThrottle)
After=multi-user.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-tdp

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT

BatteryChargeLimit.Description: Sets the battery charge-stop threshold from the Power & Limits tab (spares the cell when the laptop lives on AC — 80% is the usual longevity target). This tweak adds tuxthrottle-battery + a boot service that re-applies ~/.config/tuxthrottle/battery.json, since the kernel resets charge_control_end_threshold to 100 on every boot. No-op on a machine that doesn't expose that sysfs attribute. Reversible (service removed; threshold left wherever it currently is).
BatteryChargeLimit.check: test -x /usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-battery && systemctl is-enabled tuxthrottle-battery.service 2>/dev/null | grep -q enabled
apply:
cat > /usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-battery <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
F="${1:-/home/{USER}/.config/tuxthrottle/battery.json}"
[ -r "$F" ] || exit 0
P=$(grep -oE '"percent"[ ]*:[ ]*[0-9]+' "$F" | grep -oE '[0-9]+$')
[ -n "$P" ] || exit 0
for b in /sys/class/power_supply/BAT*/charge_control_end_threshold; do
  [ -w "$b" ] && echo "$P" > "$b"
done
exit 0
SCRIPT

cat > /etc/systemd/system/tuxthrottle-battery.service <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=Re-apply saved battery charge limit (TuxThrottle)
After=multi-user.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-battery

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT

NvidiaPowerLimit.Description: Lets the Power & Limits tab cap the RTX 3050 Ti's board power (nvidia-smi -pl) — the most effective single lever for GPU heat and battery life. Installs tuxthrottle-nvpl + a boot service that re-applies ~/.config/tuxthrottle/nvpl.json (persistence mode + power limit), plus a scoped sudoers rule. requires the NVIDIA driver. Reversible.
NvidiaPowerLimit.check: test -x /usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-nvpl && systemctl is-enabled tuxthrottle-nvpl.service 2>/dev/null | grep -q enabled
apply:
cat > /usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-nvpl <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
F="${1:-/home/{USER}/.config/tuxthrottle/nvpl.json}"
command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
[ -r "$F" ] || exit 0
W=$(grep -oE '"watts"[ ]*:[ ]*[0-9]+' "$F" | grep -oE '[0-9]+$')
[ -n "$W" ] || exit 0
nvidia-smi -pm 1 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
nvidia-smi -pl "$W" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
exit 0
SCRIPT

cat > /etc/systemd/system/tuxthrottle-nvpl.service <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=Re-apply saved NVIDIA power limit (TuxThrottle)
After=multi-user.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-nvpl

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT

GameModeBridge.Description: Installs Feral gamemode and wires its start/end hooks to the gaming-performance / gaming-balanced scripts, so launching any game with 'gamemoderun %command%' (or a Lutris/Heroic/Steam that requests GameMode) automatically flips the performance platform_profile + fan slam, and drops back when you quit. Also sets a sensible renice/softrealtime. Requires the PowerProfileScripts tweak first. Reversible.
apply: test -x /usr/local/bin/gaming-performance || { echo 'Install the PowerProfileScripts tweak first'; exit 1; }

cat > /etc/gamemode.ini <<'INI'
[general]
renice=10
softrealtime=auto
inhibit_screensaver=1

[custom]
start=/usr/local/bin/gaming-performance
end=/usr/local/bin/gaming-balanced
INI

FanCurveDaemon.Description: Runs tuxthrottle_powerd.py as a systemd service: a closed-loop fan curve (temperature → additive alienware-wmi fan boost, on the curve you draw in the Fans tab, with cool-down hysteresis) and optional AC/battery auto-switching (applies a platform_profile + ryzenadj TDP bundle when the charger is plugged/pulled). The daemon only ever ADDS airflow over the firmware curve — it can't stop a fan — and restores fully automatic control when stopped. Reads ~/.config/tuxthrottle/powerd.json live (edit it from the Fans / Power & Limits tabs). Reversible.
apply:
cat > /etc/systemd/system/tuxthrottle-powerd.service <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=TuxThrottle fan-curve + AC-switch daemon
After=multi-user.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 {TOOLKIT_DIR}/tuxthrottle_powerd.py run --user {USER}
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT

DellBatteryThreshold.Description: The G15 5515 has no kernel charge_control_end_threshold, but Dell firmware supports a 'custom' charge interval stored in NVRAM. This installs libsmbios (smbios-battery-ctl); the Power & Limits tab then sets the stop-charging percentage through it and it persists in firmware across reboots — no service needed. Undo removes the package only; any interval you set stays in firmware until you set it back to 100 %/standard.
